Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 653 PM EDT Sun Oct 25 2026

- Dry weather continues through early next week with temperatures 
slightly above normal, despite a weak and dry cold front sagging 
southward across the region tonight into Monday.  

- Potential for fog tonight mainly southern areas, with a better 
opportunity for patchy fog or low clouds developing across the Thumb 
and Tri-Cities region Monday night.

- The next appreciable chance for measurable rainfall holds off 
until Thursday, mainly for areas across the northern half of 
Southeast Michigan.

&&

.AVIATION...

Window of limited cloud cover this evening as existing cirrus 
briefly thins ahead of a weak cold front. Modest wind from the south 
during this time. This boundary will gradually sag into the region 
overnight and Monday. Existing gradient combined with renewed 
increase in cirrus will provide a notable less favorable overall 
environment for fog formation during the early hours. Despite this, 
forecast leans into persistence with expectation for at least some 
potential mainly across the Detroit corridor as winds lighten and 
thickening cloud holds off a bit later into the night. Thicker mid 
cloud to mark the early day period with the frontal passage, with a 
wind shift to northerly affording some saturation within the lower 
layers and an associated reduction in ceiling height with time 
through the time. Confidence in cigs below VFR remains low given the 
general retention of drier conditions below 3000 ft.    

D21/DTW Convection... Thunderstorms are not forecast through the TAF 
period.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low for cigs/vsby below 200 ft and/or 1/2SM this morning. 

* Low for cigs at or below 5000 ft Monday.
